“ Availability ” means, (a) at any time other
than an Availability Block Removal Period, an amount equal to (i) the lesser of (A) the Aggregate Revolving Commitment and (B) the Borrowing Base, minus (ii) the Aggregate Revolving Exposure (calculated, with
respect to any Defaulting Lender, as if such Defaulting Lender had funded its Applicable Percentage of all outstanding Borrowings), minus (iii) the Availability Block, minus (iv) Reserves, and (b) during an
Availability Block Removal Period, the amount calculated pursuant to clause (a) of this definition but without subtracting the Availability Block pursuant to subclause (iii) thereof. 
   2

“ Availability Block Removal Period ” means the period beginning on the date set forth in an Availability Block Removal Notice
and ending on the date set forth in an Availability Block Reinstatement Notice, as such notices are delivered to the Administrative Agent pursuant to and in accordance with Section  2.01(b) .

“ Borrowing Base ”
means, at any time, the sum of (a) 90% of the Borrowers’ Eligible Accounts at such time, plus (b) the lesser of (i) 75% of the Borrowers’ Eligible Inventory, at such time, valued at the lower of cost or market value,
determined on a first-in-first-out basis and (ii) the product of 85% multiplied by the Net Orderly
Liquidation Value percentage identified in the most recent Inventory appraisal ordered by the Administrative Agent multiplied by the Borrowers’ Eligible Inventory, valued at the lowest valuation thereof set forth in such Inventory
appraisal. “ Borrowing Base Certificate ” means a certificate, signed and certified as accurate and complete by a
Financial Officer of the Borrower Representative, in substantially the form of Exhibit B or another form which is acceptable to the Administrative Agent in its Permitted Discretion.

“ Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio ” means, for any period, the ratio of (i) EBITDA for such period minus Capital
Expenditures made (to the extent not already incurred in a prior period) or incurred during such period, to (ii) the sum of (A) all principal of Indebtedness of Parent and its Subsidiaries scheduled to be paid during such period (not
including (w) the final scheduled payment of the Obligations at the Maturity Date, (x) the Secured Notes at the final maturity date applicable thereto, (y) [ reserved ], or (z) Indebtedness consisting of the financing of
insurance premiums in the ordinary course of business not in excess of the amount of such premiums to the extent that such amounts are expensed and therefor reduce EBITDA), plus (B) Consolidated Net Interest Expense of Parent and its
Subsidiaries for such period, plus (C) all amounts required to be paid by Parent and its Subsidiaries on Capitalized Lease Obligations having a scheduled due date during such period.

“ Payment Conditions ” shall be deemed to be satisfied in connection with any Payment Condition Transaction if: 
 (a) no Default has occurred and is continuing or would result immediately after giving effect to such Payment Condition
Transaction; (b) immediately after giving effect to, and at all times during the thirty (30) consecutive day period
immediately preceding, the Payment Condition Transaction, the Borrowers shall have Specified Availability calculated on a pro forma basis after giving effect to such Payment Condition Transaction of not less than the greater of (1) 20% of the
Revolving Commitment and (2) $13,000,000; and (c) the Borrower Representative shall have delivered to the Administrative
Agent a certificate in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to the Administrative Agent certifying as to the items described in (a) and (b) above and attaching calculations for item (b) (provided, that the Administrative Agent may waive
the requirement to attach calculations under this sub-clause (ii) in its sole discretion). 
 Notwithstanding the foregoing, with respect to Payment Condition Transactions that are Restricted Payments made pursuant to clause
(ii)  of Section  6.11(c) and the proceeds of such Restricted Payments are used to repurchase, retire, or redeem the Parent’s Stock, the certificate described in clause (c) of this definition shall not be
required to be delivered to the Administrative Agent; provided that (i) each certificate delivered pursuant to (x)  Section  5.03(a)(ii) (to the extent a Monthly Financial Reporting Period exists) and
(y)  Section  5.03(b) , and (ii) each Compliance Certificate (if delivered pursuant to Section  5.03(a) in lieu of the certificate described in subclause (x) of the immediately preceding
clause (i)), shall contain (A) the certifications set forth in clause (c) of this definition with respect to, and (B) a certification of the aggregate amount of, all such Restricted Payments made during the period covered by t

“ ABL Priority Collateral ” shall have the meaning set forth in the Intercreditor Agreement.

“ Notes Priority Collateral ” has the meaning set forth in the Intercreditor
Agreement. “ NYFRB ” means the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

“ Permitted Liens ” means (a) Liens held by
the Administrative Agent for the benefit of the Administrative Agent and the Secured Parties, (b) Liens for unpaid taxes that either (i) are not yet delinquent, or (ii) do not constitute an Event of Default hereunder and are the
subject of Permitted Protests, (c) Liens set forth on Schedule 6.02 , (d) the interests of lessors under operating leases, (e) purchase money Liens or the interests of lessors under Capital Leases to the extent that such Liens or
interests secure Permitted Purchase Money Indebtedness and so long as such Lien attaches only to the asset purchased or acquired and the proceeds thereof, (f) Liens arising by operation of law in favor of warehousemen, landlords, carriers,
mechanics, materialmen, laborers, or suppliers, incurred in the ordinary course of Loan Parties’ business and not in connection with the borrowing of money, and which Liens either (i) are for sums not yet delinquent, or (ii) are the
subject of Permitted Protests, (g) Liens arising from deposits made in connection with obtaining worker’s compensation or other unemployment insurance, social security and other similar laws, (h) Liens or deposits to secure
performance of bids, tenders, or leases incurred in the ordinary course of Loan Parties’ business and not in connection with the borrowing of money, (i) Liens granted as security for surety, payment, performance or appeal bonds in
connection with obtaining such bonds in the ordinary course of Loan Parties’ business, (j) Liens resulting from any judgment or award that is not an Event of Default hereunder, (k) with respect to any real property, easements,
exceptions, reservations, encroachments, restrictions, rights of way, zoning restrictions and other similar title policy exceptions or encumbrances that do not materially interfere with or impair the use or operation thereof by the Loan
Parties; (l) [ reserved ]; (m) Liens securing Indebtedness permitted under Section  6.01(l) ; (n) [ reser

“ Secured Notes ” means the 6.250% Senior Secured Notes issued by the Parent under the Secured Notes Indenture.

“ Subordinated Indebtedness ” of a Person means any Indebtedness of such Person, the payment of which is subordinated to
payment of the Secured Obligations on terms reasonably satisfactory to the Administrative Agent in its Permitted Discretion.

“ Permitted Purchase Money Indebtedness ” means, as of any date of determination, Purchase Money Indebtedness outstanding as of
such date of determination not to exceed the greater of (x) $70,000,000 and (y) 5.5% of the total consolidated assets of the Loan Parties and their Subsidiaries as reflected on their balance sheet in accordance with GAAP.

[NOT FOUND: Special Permitted Investments]

“ Specified Availability ” means, at any time, the amount of Availability as calculated
pursuant to clause (a) of the definition thereof but without subtracting the Availability Block pursuant to subclause (iii) of clause (a) of the definition thereof.

findings.sourceCitation: §1.01, definition of "Availability", clause (a)(ii), incorporated by reference into the definition of "Specified Availability"
findings.proposedIrEvidence: "Specified Availability" calculationExpression subtracts a bare DEFINED_TERM_REFERENCE to "Aggregate Revolving Exposure" with no Defaulting Lender adjustment applied, and the definition's dependsOnTerms list ("Availability", "Aggregate Revolving Commitment", "Borrowing Base", "Aggregate Revolving Exposure", "Reserves") does not even mention "Defaulting Lender" or "Applicable Percentage", while sufficiency is marked COMPLETE.
findings.verifierReasoning: "Specified Availability" is expressly defined as Availability calculated 'pursuant to clause (a)' of the Availability definition (minus the Block), so it necessarily inherits clause (a)(ii)'s parenthetical instruction that Aggregate Revolving Exposure be calculated as if any Defaulting Lender had funded its Applicable Percentage of outstanding Borrowings. The proposed IR's Specified Availability formula omits this adjustment entirely - it does not appear in the expression tree nor even as a listed dependency - yet the definition is marked COMPLETE, the sufficiency level that should receive the most scrutiny. In a scenario with a Defaulting Lender, Aggregate Revolving Exposure computed without this adjustment could differ from the amount required by the source, producing a different Specified Availability figure. Because Specified Availability directly gates the dollar/percentage threshold in the "Payment Conditions" test, this could change whether a Payment Condition Transaction is determined to be permitted, making the omission potentially material. The related "Availability" definition at least lists Defaulting Lender/Applicable Percentage as dependencies (though still not applying them in the formula) and is honestly marked PARTIAL/UNSUPPORTED for unrelated reasons; Specified Availability received no such disclosure at all.

findings.sourceEvidence: (b) the lesser of (i) 75% of the Borrowers’ Eligible Inventory, at such time, valued at the lower of cost or market value, determined on a first-in-first-out basis and (ii) the product of 85% multiplied by the Net Orderly Liquidation Value percentage identified in the most recent Inventory appraisal ... multiplied by the Borrowers’ Eligible Inventory, valued at the lowest valuation thereof set forth in such Inventory appraisal.
findings.proposedIrEvidence: Both prongs of the MIN operand multiply their respective percentages by the same generic DEFINED_TERM_REFERENCE "Eligible Inventory" (exprId ir-expr:628ed736a168df55d0cbe289 used identically in both branches), with no distinct valuation-basis modifier (lower of cost/market FIFO vs. lowest appraisal valuation) attached to either occurrence, while sufficiency is marked COMPLETE.
findings.verifierReasoning: The source text explicitly instructs that the same underlying Eligible Inventory pool is to be valued differently for purposes of each of the two prongs of the lesser-of test - cost/market FIFO basis for prong (i) versus lowest appraisal valuation for prong (ii) - which is the classic mechanism that makes the two prongs produce genuinely different dollar amounts. The proposed IR references the identical "Eligible Inventory" defined term in both prongs without capturing that distinction. If the base "Eligible Inventory" definition elsewhere in the instrument does not already encode these alternate valuation bases, the compiled formula could compute a materially different Borrowing Base than the source requires. I cannot fully resolve this from the evidence available (the substantive "Eligible Inventory" definition was not supplied to me), so I flag it as uncertain rather than confirmed, but it is a real candidate discrepancy in a definition marked COMPLETE.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: numerator is a plain SUBTRACT of METRIC_REFERENCE "EBITDA" minus METRIC_REFERENCE "Capital Expenditures" with no representation of the 'to the extent not already incurred in a prior period' timing/double-counting proviso, and sufficiency is marked COMPLETE.
findings.verifierReasoning: The source includes a specific timing qualifier designed to prevent double-counting of capital expenditures that were incurred in an earlier period but paid/made in the measured period. The proposed IR collapses this into a bare metric subtraction without any indication that the timing proviso is being applied (either inside the 'Capital Expenditures' metric definition, which was not supplied, or via some other mechanism). Because this could change the numerator in periods where capex timing differs from incurrence, it is a plausible, if narrow, omission in a definition marked COMPLETE rather than PARTIAL.
